m.chalisa.cau1: O hero of the Raghus, benefactor of devotees; Lord, please hear our plea.
m.chalisa.cau2: Whoever meditates on you night and day, no other devotee is his equal.
m.chalisa.cau3: Śiva meditates on you in his mind; Brahmā and Indra do not reach your end.
m.chalisa.cau4: Victory, victory, victory to you, compassionate Lord of the Raghus; ever protect the saints.
m.chalisa.cau5: Your messenger is the hero Hanumān, whose power the three worlds know.
m.chalisa.cau6: Your staff-like arms are mighty, O compassionate one; you killed Rāvaṇa and protected the gods.
m.chalisa.cau7: You are the lord of the masterless, O Master; you are ever the helper of the humble.
m.chalisa.cau8: Even Brahmā and the others do not reach your end; O Lord, they ever sing your glory.
m.chalisa.cau9: All four Vedas bear witness that you have kept the honour of your devotees.
m.chalisa.cau10: Sarasvatī sings your virtues in her mind; Indra, lord of the gods, does not reach their end.
m.chalisa.cau11: Whoever takes your name, no one else is as blessed as he.
m.chalisa.cau12: The name of Rāma is boundless; all four Vedas have proclaimed it aloud.
m.chalisa.cau13: Gaṇapati took your name, and you made him the first to be worshipped.
m.chalisa.cau14: Śeṣa ever repeats your name; he has borne the weight of the earth on his head.
m.chalisa.cau15: That weight stays as light as a flower to him; no one reaches your end.
m.chalisa.cau16: Bharata held your name in his heart; so he was never defeated in battle.
m.chalisa.cau17: Your name shines in Śatrughna's heart; at its remembrance the enemy is destroyed.
m.chalisa.cau18: Lakṣmaṇa is obedient to you; he ever stands guard over the saints.
m.chalisa.cau19: So no one can win against him in battle, even if Yama himself joins the fight.
m.chalisa.cau20: Mahālakṣmī has taken incarnation; in every way she reduces sin to ashes.
m.chalisa.cau21: Her holy name was sung as Sītā; she showed the power of Bhuvaneśvarī.
m.chalisa.cau22: She came forth from a pot; seeing her, the moon is put to shame.
m.chalisa.cau23: She ever presses your feet; all nine treasures lie at your feet.
m.chalisa.cau24: The eighteen auspicious siddhis give themselves up to you.
m.chalisa.cau25: And whatever many other powers of lordship there are, O lord of Sītā, you alone made them.
m.chalisa.cau26: By your will, creating countless worlds takes not a moment's delay.
m.chalisa.cau27: Whoever fixes his mind on your feet surely attains liberation.
m.chalisa.cau28: Victory, victory, victory to you, Lord, whose form is light, the attributeless Brahman, undivided and incomparable.
m.chalisa.cau29: O Lord, true, true, and true to your vow, you are the true, the eternal, the indweller.
m.chalisa.cau30: Whoever sings your praise in truth surely gains the four fruits (dharma, wealth, desire and liberation).
m.chalisa.cau31: Śiva, the lord of Gaurī, has sworn a true oath that through devotion you have granted every siddhi.
m.chalisa.cau32: Listen, Rāma: you are our father; Bharata proclaimed you alone worthy of worship in the family.
m.chalisa.cau33: You, O God, are our family deity; you are our revered teacher, dear as life.
m.chalisa.cau34: Whatever may be, you alone are king. Victory, victory, victory, Lord: keep our honour.
m.chalisa.cau35: Rāma, you nourish the soul; victory, victory, victory to you, darling of Daśaratha.
m.chalisa.cau36: You who are knowledge itself, give knowledge to the heart. I bow, I bow to you; victory to you, king and lord of the world.
m.chalisa.cau37: Blessed, blessed are you, and blessed is your glory! Your name takes away anguish.
m.chalisa.cau38: The gods with their own mouths sang of you as true and pure; kettledrums sounded and conches were blown.
m.chalisa.cau39: True, true are you, true and eternal; you alone are our body, mind and wealth.
m.chalisa.cau40: Whoever recites this, knowledge dawns in his heart.
m.chalisa.cau41: His coming and going in birth and death ends; Śiva holds this word of mine true.
m.chalisa.cau42: And whatever other hope he has in his mind, he gains the fruit his heart desires.
m.chalisa.cau43: Those who meditate on you at the three times of day, and offer tulasī leaves and flowers,
m.chalisa.cau44: and set greens and leaves before you as food, gain every perfection.
m.chalisa.cau45: At the end he goes to the city of Śrī Rāma, where, being born, he is called a devotee of Hari.
m.chalisa.cau46: Śrī Haridāsa tells it and sings it: he goes to the abode of Vaikuṇṭha.
m.chalisa.do1: Whoever keeps the observance and recites this for seven days with his mind fixed on it, says Haridāsa, surely gains devotion by Hari's grace.
m.chalisa.do2: Whoever reads the Rāma Chālīsā with his mind fixed on Śrī Rāma's feet, whatever wish he makes in his mind is all fulfilled.
